content.text:
Confirmed: [discussion #13082](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13082) is a real mise bug, not an activation problem or user configuration error. It remains present on current `main` (`668286e88`).

Cause:

- `depends` tasks are resolved before execution and included in the task-tool installation pass ([run.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/9631/mise/src/cli/run.rs:713), [task_tool_installer.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/9631/mise/src/task/task_tool_installer.rs:26)).
- `{ task = "…" }` entries are intentionally resolved later, while their parent is executing ([task_executor.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/9631/mise/src/task/task_executor.rs:886)).
- The injected task graph is constructed only after all initial tool installation has completed ([task_executor.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/9631/mise/src/task/task_executor.rs:965)).
- Its environment correctly includes the task-specific tool once installed, explaining why the second invocation succeeds.

The documentation promises that task-level tools are installed before their task runs ([task-configuration.md](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/9631/mise/docs/tasks/task-configuration.md:308)), so this behavior contradicts the intended contract.

Recommended fix: after `inject_and_wait` constructs `sub_deps`, install the tools required by that injected graph before sending it to the scheduler. This is safer than statically treating `run` references as dependencies because run entries may be templated, sequential, wildcarded, or point into monorepo subprojects.

Regression coverage should include:

- A single `{ task = "child" }` whose child declares `tools.tiny`.
- A `{ tasks = [...] }` group.
- An injected child with dependencies requiring their own tools.
- Preservation of `--skip-tools`, disabled auto-install, and dry-run behavior.

This appears to be a longstanding gap dating back to sub-tasks in run lists, rather than a regression introduced by version `2026.9.5`. No code or GitHub comment was changed.
make a pr, post a reply

I’ll implement the fix at the dynamic task-injection boundary, add focused regression coverage (including `--skip-tools`), run the relevant checks, then open a ready-for-review PR and reply to the discussion with the diagnosis and PR link.
